skill.name: mcp-server
skill.description: Guide for building MCP servers that expose external services through well-designed tools. It covers Python FastMCP, Node and TypeScript SDK patterns, testing, and evaluation workflows.
skill.summary: Build MCP servers with clear tools, safe API patterns, and practical evaluations.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: The static findings are overwhelmingly documentation examples, placeholder credentials, or TypeScript string templates, so I marked them false positive. The active scripts do include a legitimate evaluation harness that can launch a user-selected MCP server command, which creates a bounded local execution risk. No evidence found of prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or malicious secret harvesting in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness launches a command supplied by the user.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must run only trusted local MCP server commands, and consider validating command paths in shared environments.

remediation.issue: The harness passes explicit environment variables to the evaluated MCP subprocess.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to pass only credentials intended for that server and avoid using production secrets in evaluations.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder tokens that resemble real secret formats.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly fake placeholders such as YOUR_TOKEN_HERE and avoid realistic prefixes in examples.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled MCP Server Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation CLI accepts a command and arguments for stdio transport, then passes them into StdioServerParameters to launch the MCP server. This is intended for local evaluation, but running untrusted commands can execute arbitrary local code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command, args, and env values come from CLI arguments and are passed into the MCP stdio client. The surrounding code is an evaluation harness, so the risk depends on running trusted inputs.

content.value_statement: MCP server projects often fail because tools mirror APIs instead of real workflows. This skill guides planning, implementation, testing, and evaluation for agent-friendly MCP servers.
actual_capabilities: Plans MCP tools around complete user workflows instead of raw API endpoints.
Explains Python FastMCP implementation patterns with Pydantic validation.
Explains Node and TypeScript implementation patterns with Zod validation.
Shows response formatting, pagination, truncation, and error handling practices.
Provides an evaluation workflow and a script-based MCP server test harness.
limitations: It is a guide and harness, not a finished MCP server for a specific service.
It requires the user to supply API details, credentials, and service-specific logic.
The evaluation harness needs valid Anthropic credentials to run model-based tests.
Remote documentation links may change after the skill package was published.

best_practices: Design tools around complete tasks that agents need to finish.
Use strict input validation and clear, actionable error messages.
Keep responses concise, paginated, and easy for models to compare.
anti_patterns: Do not wrap every API endpoint as a separate MCP tool without workflow design.
Do not return large raw payloads when filtered summaries would answer the task.
Do not run evaluation commands or servers from untrusted sources.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete MCP server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and an evaluation harness for building your own server.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and Node or TypeScript with the MCP SDK.

faq.question: Can it connect to external APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide explains API client patterns, authentication planning, pagination, and error handling.

faq.question: Does the evaluation harness require credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Model-based evaluation requires a valid Anthropic API key and any service credentials your MCP server needs.

faq.question: Is it safe to run any command with the harness?
faq.answer: No. Only run trusted local MCP server commands, because the harness can start a process you specify.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is suitable for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows.
